identificationModule.briefTitle: Oral Ivermectin for Chikungunya Viral Infection
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Oral Ivermectin for Patients With Chikungunya Viral Infection During Urban Outbreak in Southern Thailand

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Chikungunya viral infection (CVI) is a mosquito-borne infection, caused by chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an alphavirus, belonging to the family Togaviridae. This infection causes febrile illness associated with high fever, rash, acute deliberating and persistent arthralgia. There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for this infection. Ivermectin (IVM), commonly-used antiparasitic, has been demonstrated to inhibit replication of CHIKV.

armGroups.label: Patients received oral ivermectin, adjunctive to conventional treatment

interventions.name: Ivermectin
interventions.description: 3-day 1 daily dose of 400 μg/kg oral ivermectin
armGroupLabels: Patients received oral ivermectin, adjunctive to conventional treatment

primaryOutcomes.description: 120 participants would be under Body Temperature Assessment - the staff would assess once daily until the fever clearance was below 38C and the measure proportion of patients with fever clearance in each day of assessment until fever clearance at least in 7 days

secondaryOutcomes.description: 120 participants would be obtained blood examination for virological testing every day until virological clearance at least in 7 days

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* patients with virologic confirmation of chikungunya infection who had symptoms less than 72 hours prior to visit

Exclusion Criteria:

* patients with virologic confirmation of chikungunya infection who had symptoms more than 72 hours prior to visit
